text:
maria: heads-up — noticed schema_reject_rate_by_route spiking for /v1/invoke on canary-variant-3 :eyes:

jake: saw that too. looks like most rejects are from fncall responses including an extra top-level `meta` obj the validator flags as unknown

anya: do we have examples? can we surface top examples in the console instead of raw counts? that's what PM asked for

sam-dev: pasted a sanitized snippet from logs:
```json
{"tool_result": {"status":"ok","output":"..."}, "meta": {"source":"legacy-adapter","ver":"0.9"}}
```

maria: exact. validator expects `{tool_result: object}` not `{tool_result, meta}` so strict mode rejects. but most of these `meta` fields are harmless and originated from an older connector

ops-alyssa: this is worrying because sampling policy currently picks rejects uniformly. we might be over-indexing on legacy noise -> false alarm in canary metrics

jake: agree. proposal: change sampling to 2-stage — 1) sample a small percentage of accepts for baseline, 2) sample rejects with stratification by connector/source header. that should reduce observer bias

anya: +1. also from UX side, add "Top 3 mismatch snippets" in the route drilldown and a quick toggle: show accepts vs rejects examples. PM wants to see root-cause without running queries

sam-dev: implementation note: validator returns `reject_reason` currently as free-text. can we normalize to codes e.g. `UNKNOWN_FIELD_META`, `TYPE_MISMATCH` so dashboard buckets are stable?

maria: yes please. normalizing helps both telemetry and the rollouts UI. we'll need a lightweight mapping from freetext -> code to backfill historical events for the dashboard

ops-alyssa: regarding billing: some of the rejected runs are still billed. customers see surprising charges when we fallback to degen. we should add `reject_handling` field in logs: `fallbacked_to_model_variant` | `returned_error` | `coerced`

jake: good call. that also helps audit when strict validate is enabled per-customer. add route-level flag in console so SREs can toggle `strict_schema` per-route for canaries

anya: UX: show a warning badge when strict is on and link to example rejects + cost impact estimate (last 24h)

sam-dev: quick dev plan:
- validator: emit `reject_code` and `reject_meta` (adapter id) (PR1)
- telemetry: add `schema_reject_sampling_stage` tag (accept_baseline|reject_stratified) (PR2)
- console: top-3 snippets + toggle + cost estimate (PR3)

maria: timeline? we need this before we widen canary-variant-3 to 100% in EU region next week

jake: I can do PR1 by EOD tomorrow, PR2 Wednesday. PR3 needs design input from @anya — can you mock the widget by Tue?

anya: will mock today/tomorrow AM. will include sample toggle states and an example cost tooltip

ops-alyssa: one more thing: sampling rates. propose defaults: accepts baseline 0.5%, rejects stratified 5% per-source, but cap total sampled logs to 20k/day per-org to control storage

maria: sounds reasonable. make the rates configurable per-org with sane defaults

jake: I'll add config and admin route to adjust per-org limits. also will add an internal metric `schema_sampling_overflow` so we know when cap hits and UI shows partial visibility

qa_bot: FYI — existing regex-based example filter will drop any snippets with PII; keep that in place. tests will run on sanitized examples only

sam-dev: final: can we add a small migration to map old freetext reject reasons into new `reject_code` buckets so historical dashboard doesn't break?

maria: yes — create a backfill job that runs hourly and tags historical events with predicted code. add a label `backfill_v1` until done

anya: I'll include an "examples" panel mock and the cost calc in the mock. once we have a working PR we can preview in staging

maria: thanks everyone. action items summarized: Jake PR1/PR2, Anya mock PR3, Sam-dev handle log fields + backfill plan, Ops set sampling caps, QA verifies sanitization. ping me when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
